en: Abstract
zh: 摘要

en: In late-socialist Romania, the state sought to govern economic crisis by demanding market-like conduct from cultural institutions while continuing to bind them to the political structures of socialism. Drawing on archival planning reports, media accounts, and post-socialist recollections, this article traces the emergence of a “self-financing regime” that reorganized cultural production around revenue generation, entrepreneurial conduct, and managerial accountability. I argue that self-financing constituted neither a retreat of socialism nor an incipient transition to capitalism, but an experiment in governing crisis by relocating the burdens of economic survival onto institutions themselves. This shift generated a contradictory institutional world: cultural actors were compelled to pursue economic self-sufficiency and become self-optimizing subjects even as markets remained ideologically repudiated, socialist obligations endured, and nominal decentralization extended bureaucratic oversight. Yet contradiction did not simply signal the incoherence of late socialism. As these tensions became embedded in everyday institutional practice, contradiction provided the very means through which austerity was rendered governable. The Romanian case thus shows how market-like rationalities could emerge from within socialist crisis management and crystallize into historically distinct forms of governance. By situating these entanglements before the so-called “end of history,” the article unsettles teleological narratives of socialist-capitalist rupture and reconsiders crisis as a historically contingent site where seemingly opposed political-economic logics can be made and remade in practice.
zh: 在社会主义晚期的罗马尼亚，国家试图要求文化机构采取类似市场的行为来治理经济危机，同时继续将其约束于社会主义的政治结构。本文利用档案中的计划报告、媒体报道以及后社会主义时期的回忆，追溯一种‘自筹经费体制’的形成；这一体制围绕创收、企业家式行为和管理问责重新组织了文化生产。我认为，自筹经费既不意味着社会主义的退却，也不是向资本主义过渡的开端，而是一场将经济生存负担转移给机构自身、借此治理危机的实验。这一转变产生了一个充满矛盾的制度世界：文化行动者被迫追求经济自足，成为不断优化自身的主体，而市场在意识形态上仍遭否认，社会主义义务依然存在，名义上的分权又扩大了官僚监督。然而，矛盾并不只是社会主义晚期缺乏一致性的征兆。当这些张力嵌入机构的日常实践时，矛盾本身便成了使紧缩得以治理的手段。因此，罗马尼亚的案例显示，类似市场的理性可以从社会主义危机管理内部产生，并凝结为具有特定历史形态的治理形式。本文将这些相互纠缠的关系放在所谓‘历史终结’之前考察，以此动摇将社会主义与资本主义描述为目的论式断裂的叙事，并重新把危机理解为一个具有历史偶然性的场域：在这里，看似对立的政治经济逻辑能够在实践中被创造和重塑。

en: Introduction
zh: 引言

en: In a 1979 Communist Party committee meeting, Nicolae Ceaușescu declared, “We should stop making Romanian films if they don’t generate income, artists should be paid from the film’s revenue, like everywhere else in the world. Romanian cinema must become financially self-sustaining in and of itself.”

His statement captured a constitutive tension at the heart of late-socialist cultural governance: an institutional configuration that demanded market-oriented conduct, in which artistic value was required to demonstrate economic viability while remaining embedded in a system that formally disavowed market logic.
zh: 在1979年的一次共产党委员会会议上，尼古拉·齐奥塞斯库宣称：‘如果罗马尼亚电影不能创造收入，我们就应该停止拍摄；艺术家应当从电影收入中取得报酬，世界上其他地方都是如此。罗马尼亚电影必须凭借自身实现财务上的自我维持。’
这番话抓住了社会主义晚期文化治理核心的一种构成性张力：这种制度安排要求采取面向市场的行为，艺术价值必须证明其经济上的可行性，却又始终嵌入一个在形式上否认市场逻辑的体制之中。

en: By the time socialism had reached the brink of collapse, cultural institutions were already curbing dependence on state subsidies, translating their activities into measures of economic performance, and cultivating practices of financial self-reliance under conditions of austerity. Contrary to customary ideological framing, this transformation produced market-oriented logics within socialist governance long before any formal transition to the market, which gave shape to a distinct mode of cultural governance in which financial accountability became an internal principle of institutional life. Using an abductive approach, I trace moments where socialist state-planned governance and capitalist, market-like valuation logics intersected in practice, and where formal directives collided with everyday improvisation.
At the center of this analysis is the self-financing regime imposed on cultural institutions, an “almost capitalist” fulcrum of economic behavior in a socialist economy.

The measures taken in service of this reconfiguration were neither accidental by-products of austerity nor premature signs of transition toward capitalism, but integral to a framework that reorganized cultural institutional life under late socialism by negotiating its own contradictions and rendering them both operational and opaque.
zh: 当社会主义走到崩溃边缘时，文化机构早已开始减少对国家补贴的依赖，将自身活动转化为经济绩效指标，并在紧缩条件下培养财务自立的实践。有别于惯常的意识形态叙述，这一转变远在正式转向市场之前，就在社会主义治理内部产生了市场取向的逻辑，由此形成一种独特的文化治理模式：财务问责成为机构生活的内在原则。我采用溯因方法，追踪社会主义国家计划治理与资本主义式、类似市场的价值评估逻辑在实践中交会的时刻，以及正式指令与日常临机应变相冲突的场景。
分析的核心是强加给文化机构的自筹经费体制：它是社会主义经济中一个‘近乎资本主义’的经济行为支点。
服务于这种重组的措施，既不是紧缩偶然带来的副产品，也不是向资本主义转型的早期征兆；它们属于一个完整框架，这一框架通过应对自身矛盾、使矛盾既可运作又不易看清，重新组织了社会主义晚期的文化机构生活。

en: Archival evidence concerning philharmonics, museums, and other cultural institutions reveals that artists and administrators devised ingenious strategies to keep cultural production afloat, often in ways that unsettle prevailing assumptions about how socialism and capitalism were thought to operate before the “end of history.”

Much of the scholarship on state socialism has traditionally been organized around oppositional interpretive categories (state versus society, repression versus freedom, ideology versus resistance), which have shaped understandings of cultural life through prisms of ideology and censorship or artistic autonomy and dissent.

Yet such frameworks tend to obscure a more consequential transformation that was unfolding at the level of organizational rationality itself, where hybrid governing logics became entangled in practice.
zh: 有关爱乐乐团、博物馆及其他文化机构的档案证据表明，艺术家和管理者设计出各种巧妙策略来维持文化生产，而这些做法常常动摇人们对于‘历史终结’之前社会主义与资本主义如何运作的通行假设。
有关国家社会主义的许多研究，传统上围绕相互对立的解释范畴展开：国家与社会、压制与自由、意识形态与抵抗。这些范畴使人们从意识形态和审查，或艺术自主和异议的角度理解文化生活。
然而，这些框架往往遮蔽了一个更具深远影响的转变：转变发生在组织理性本身的层面，各种混合的治理逻辑在那里于实践中相互缠结。

en: An important qualification is necessary in this context. As scholars of socialist political economy such as János Kornai, Martha Lampland, and Katherine Verdery have shown, socialist economies long incorporated mechanisms of revenue generation and enterprise responsibility, even if these operated under distinct property relations and budgetary conditions.

If economic calculation was not foreign to socialism, then the significance of the Romanian case lies elsewhere: in how a crisis-ridden socialist state that continued to affirm the primacy of centralized planning progressively redefined culture through economic accountability. Under the pressure of austerity and broader crisis, economic performance ceased to be merely a technique of administration and became a principle of cultural evaluation. What was increasingly at stake, as a result, was how cultural value, professional legitimacy, and even institutional survival came to be assessed and made governable through the economic language of measurable outcome.
zh: 这里有必要作一项重要限定。正如亚诺什·科尔奈、玛莎·兰普兰和凯瑟琳·韦尔德里等社会主义政治经济学研究者所表明的，社会主义经济长期以来就包含创收机制和企业责任机制，只是它们是在不同的产权关系和预算条件下运作。
如果经济计算并非社会主义的外来物，那么罗马尼亚案例的意义就在别处：一个危机缠身、仍坚持中央计划优先地位的社会主义国家，如何通过经济问责逐步重新界定文化。在紧缩和更广泛危机的压力下，经济绩效不再仅仅是一种行政管理技术，而成为文化评价的原则。于是，日益关键的问题便是：文化价值、职业正当性，甚至机构的存续，如何通过关于可衡量结果的经济语言接受评估，并被纳入治理。

en: Therefore, rather than invoking capitalism as a totalizing category or casting late socialism as an inevitable march toward it—where socialism seamlessly collapsed into capitalism, ending ideological debate and “history” itself—the analysis reconstructs the hybrid institutional logics that made cultural governance and institutional rationalities operational prior to socialism’s demise. It traces how macro-political reforms (such as the self-financing regime) were articulated at the level of policy discourse and operationalized by central authorities. Furthermore, to understand how contradictions played out in practice, it then turns to how market-oriented logics materialized in the everyday operations of cultural institutions. Moving between these registers—policy deployed from above and practice enacted from below—the analysis shows how cultural governance functioned through the managed coexistence of clashing logics and rationalities. In this frictional space of hybridity, culture had to learn to sustain itself, and in doing so, it also worked
rather than resolved the contradictory conditions that structured its survival.
zh: 因此，本分析并不把资本主义当作囊括一切的范畴，也不把社会主义晚期写成必然通向资本主义的历程——仿佛社会主义无缝地瓦解为资本主义，从而终结意识形态争论以及‘历史’本身——而是重建社会主义消亡之前，使文化治理及机构理性能够实际运作的混合制度逻辑。它追踪宏观政治改革，例如自筹经费体制，如何在政策话语层面得到阐述，并由中央当局付诸实施。进一步说，为理解矛盾在实践中如何展开，分析随后转向市场取向的逻辑如何在文化机构的日常运作中具体呈现。通过在这些层面之间移动，即自上而下部署的政策与自下而上实行的实践，分析揭示文化治理如何通过对相互冲突的逻辑与理性的共存加以管理而运作。在这一充满摩擦的混合空间里，文化必须学会自我维持；在此过程中，它也
那些塑造其生存的矛盾条件，而不是将其消解。

en: To untangle this empirical knot, I draw on a wide range of archival planning reports, administrative decrees, institutional statutes, and policy documents from the National State Archive of Romania and the legal gazette of Romania (

). I also draw from news bulletins and feature stories archived by the Arcanum database. Although such media archives are often dismissed as mere extensions of party propaganda, they offer more than their official veneer suggests. Embedded within them are fragments of grassroots reporting, micro-level interviews, and site-specific voices of discontent—sources that, when read “along the archival grain,” illuminate intersections of domination and adaptation.

While my analysis centers on the final decade of socialism (1980–1989), earlier episodes are folded in to show how market logics were systematically and intentionally incorporated into socialist frameworks long before the crisis of the 1980s. Additionally, I weave post-socialist recollections into the narrative, since such testimonies reveal how cultural actors retrospectively made sense of their lived experiences during late socialism.
zh: 为解开这一经验材料中的纠结，我广泛使用罗马尼亚国家档案馆和罗马尼亚法律公报（
）中的计划报告、行政法令、机构章程及政策文件，也利用Arcanum数据库收录的新闻简报和专题报道。虽然这些媒体档案常被视为党宣传的简单延伸而遭忽视，它们提供的内容却比官方表象所显示的更多。其中嵌有基层报道的片段、微观访谈以及具体地点上表达不满的声音；‘顺着档案的纹理’阅读这些材料，就能照见支配与适应的交会。
尽管我的分析聚焦社会主义的最后十年，即1980—1989年，我也纳入更早的事件，以说明早在1980年代危机之前，市场逻辑就已被系统地、有意识地引入社会主义框架。此外，我将后社会主义时期的回忆织入叙事，因为这类证言揭示了文化行动者如何回过头来理解他们在社会主义晚期的生活经验。

en: This nonlinear, longue durée perspective prioritizes continuities and sedimented logics over ahistorical fantasies of rupture. Drawing on a historical sociological perspective, I read the archives relationally in order to make visible how institutions, policies, and cultural actors co-constituted one another under crisis conditions and produced hybrid modes of organization. If decrees and transcripts of closed-door meetings codified norms from above, reports and news bulletins reveal how the prescriptions were negotiated and refracted in practice. I treat these records not as transparent windows into distant or exotic pasts but as situated sites of practice. In addition to documenting official directives and performing state narratives, they also expose frictions and enable the reconstruction of the micro-level mechanisms through which policies were implemented or repurposed on the ground.
zh: 这一非线性的长时段视角，将连续性与沉积下来的逻辑置于关于断裂的非历史幻想之上。我从历史社会学视角出发，以关系性的方式阅读档案，使人们看见机构、政策与文化行动者如何在危机条件下彼此构成，并生产出混合的组织方式。如果说法令和闭门会议记录从上层规定了规范，那么报告和新闻简报则揭示这些规定如何在实践中被协商并发生折射。我不把这些记录当作通向遥远或异域过去的透明窗口，而将其视为处于具体情境中的实践场所。它们既记录官方指令、展演国家叙事，也暴露摩擦，使我们能够重建政策在基层被实施或改变用途的微观机制。

en: To grasp how late socialism experimented with market-oriented forms of governance in the cultural sector, I propose an analytic framework attuned to these hybrid and often contradictory logics. The article identifies four constitutive contradictions of the self-financing regime, which manifest empirically as a series of institutional paradoxes. First, I explore how market rationality was inscribed without markets: cultural outputs were stratified by perceived commercial potential, and institutions were assessed through metrics of efficiency and self-generated income even as market infrastructures remained largely absent. Second, I examine entrepreneurial socialism as both policy and practice, in which cultural administrators, musicians, and pedagogues were encouraged to act entrepreneurially and enact a logic that remained ideologically suspect. Third, I reveal how state socialism sought to remedy the lack of entrepreneurial disposition through specialized retraining programs and thereby produced a distinctive hybrid of economic rationality and political loyalty that transformed cultural management from within. Fourth, I show how the promised decentralization produced its bureaucratic counterpart. Instead of enabling creative autonomy, it generated onerous paperwork and epistemic surveillance that imposed novel forms of individual accountability aimed at shoring up institutional budgets.
zh: 为了把握社会主义晚期如何在文化部门试验面向市场的治理形式，我提出一个关注这些混合且往往相互矛盾的逻辑的分析框架。本文辨识自筹经费体制中的四种构成性矛盾，它们在经验层面表现为一系列制度悖论。第一，我探讨市场理性如何在没有市场的情况下被写入制度：文化产出依据其被认为具有的商业潜力分层，机构依据效率和自主创收的指标接受评估，而市场基础设施却仍在很大程度上缺席。第二，我考察作为政策和实践的企业家式社会主义：文化管理者、音乐家和教育工作者被鼓励以企业家方式行事，实行一种在意识形态上仍受怀疑的逻辑。第三，我揭示国家社会主义如何试图通过专门的再培训项目弥补企业家倾向的不足，由此产生经济理性与政治忠诚的一种独特混合，从内部改造文化管理。第四，我说明承诺中的分权如何产生其官僚主义的对应物。它没有带来创作自主，而是生成繁重的文书工作与知识层面的监视，以新型个人问责来支撑机构预算。

en: These four paradoxes are not symmetrical in scope or function. Analytically, they point to constitutive contradictions within the self-financing regime; empirically, they appeared as paradoxical configurations through which institutions experienced and negotiated demands. While the first paradox traces how these contradictions were articulated and deployed from above, the other three capture their ambivalent afterlives: simultaneous outcomes of policy and situated, improvised responses through which institutions navigated—and at times subverted—those very directives. In line with my abductive approach, each subsection begins with an archival puzzle that makes the contradictions of self-financing empirically tractable.
zh: 这四种悖论的范围和功能并不对称。在分析层面，它们指向自筹经费体制内部的构成性矛盾；在经验层面，它们表现为悖论式的配置，机构通过这些配置经历并协商各种要求。第一种悖论追踪这些矛盾如何从上层被表述和部署，另外三种则把握其含混的后续影响：它们既是政策产生的结果，也是机构在具体情境中临机作出的回应，机构借此应付、并有时颠覆同一套指令。与我的溯因方法相一致，每一小节都从一个档案谜题开始，使自筹经费的矛盾能够得到经验层面的具体分析。

en: Market Rationality Without Markets: Differentiated Sectors and Incremental Reform
zh: 没有市场的市场理性：差异化部门与渐进改革

en: Among the archival traces documenting Romania’s late socialist turn to self-financing, one testimony captures its contradictions with particular clarity. Constantin Ungureanu, director of the Craiova Opera in the 1980s, recalled the challenges that arose once the institution ceased to receive full state subsidies. By January 1984, salaries could only be paid at 80 percent, and by April, the performance capacity of the institution had plummeted to 25 percent. “To achieve what was demanded,” he noted, “I calculated we would need six full-house performances a day. An absurdity. We tried every way we could to make ends meet. We even did five shows a day on the road, touring to bring in money.” Shortly afterward, Ungureanu was dismissed: “I was told we should try with other, more merchant-like people.”
zh: 在记录罗马尼亚社会主义晚期转向自筹经费的档案痕迹中，一份证言格外清晰地抓住了它的矛盾。1980年代克拉约瓦歌剧院院长康斯坦丁·温古雷亚努回忆了该机构不再获得国家全额补贴后遭遇的困难。到1984年1月，工资只能支付80%；到4月，机构的演出能力骤降到25%。他指出：‘为了完成要求，我算过，我们每天需要演六场，而且场场满座。荒谬。我们想尽办法维持收支。我们甚至每天在外面演五场，靠巡演挣钱。’不久之后，温古雷亚努被解职：‘他们告诉我，应该试试其他更像商人的人。’

en: As this testimony indicates, institutions were pushed into seemingly impossible calculations of viability, where intensified demands for efficiency and output clashed with preexisting definitions of what cultural work was. Introduced under the banners of austerity and a “rational use of resources,”

this logic took the form of a top-down reordering of institutional life that curtailed expenditure and quantified performance, generating forms of economic rationalization that coexisted with, rather than displaced, socialist governance. Within these conditions of material constraint and metricized performance, composer and critic Valentin Petculescu recalls numerous “unpaid concerts, with rehearsals at skating-rink temperatures,” conditions that led instrumentalists to what they came to call, not without irony, the “invention of the decade”: fingerless gloves, devised to allow performance in extreme cold.
zh: 正如这份证言所示，机构被推入看似不可能的生存计算：对效率和产出的强化要求，同既有的文化工作定义发生冲突。这套逻辑以紧缩和‘合理利用资源’之名引入，
采取自上而下重整机构生活的形式，压缩支出、量化绩效，形成与社会主义治理并存而非取代它的经济合理化方式。在这种物质受限、绩效指标化的条件下，作曲家兼评论家瓦伦丁·佩特库列斯库回忆起许多‘没有报酬的音乐会，以及在溜冰场般的温度中进行的排练’。这些条件促使器乐演奏者创造了他们不无讽刺地称作‘十年间的发明’的东西：为了能在严寒中演奏而做出的露指手套。

en: Yet these anecdotes of everyday improvisation were not mere ad hoc responses to austerity. The self-financing regime itself emerged from a broader reconfiguration of socialist governance under the pressures of global financial crisis and Romania’s mounting external debt. By 1982, this debt had become unsustainable and prompted negotiations with the International Monetary Fund. In pursuit of economic sovereignty, Ceaușescu turned toward a unilateral strategy of accelerated debt repayment and intensified austerity, giving rise to a
regime characterized by draconian internal constraints and a sweeping reorganization of administrative and economic governance across the socialist economy.

Within this framework, logics of self-financing, decentralized managerial responsibility, and performance-based accountability were put into operation. They were not confined to the cultural sector but circulated across domains such as education, healthcare, or agro-industrial administration albeit with different intensities and institutional configurations. Ceaușescu himself framed the self-financing regime as a “unified development program,” insisting that all administrative units across the socialist economy operate under the principle that they should not “spend more than the resources [they] generate.”
zh: 然而，这些关于日常应变的轶事并不只是对紧缩的临时反应。自筹经费体制本身，产生于全球金融危机和罗马尼亚不断攀升的外债压力下社会主义治理的更广泛重组。到1982年，外债已不可持续，促使罗马尼亚与国际货币基金组织谈判。为追求经济主权，齐奥塞斯库转向单方面加速偿债、强化紧缩的战略，由此形成一种
的体制：它以严酷的内部约束，以及横跨社会主义经济的行政和经济治理全面重组为特征。
在这一框架下，自筹经费、分散化的管理责任和以绩效为基础的问责逻辑被投入运作。它们并不限于文化部门，也流通于教育、医疗和农业工业管理等领域，只是强度与制度配置有所不同。齐奥塞斯库本人把自筹经费体制表述为一个‘统一的发展计划’，坚持要求社会主义经济中的所有行政单位遵循这样一项原则：不得‘花费超过[自身]所创造的资源’。

en: Within this broader economic reorientation, the self-financing regime became a key instrument for both legitimizing austerity and increasing fiscal extraction capacity. Designed to make institutions (partially) responsible for their own budgets, it shifted the burden of economic viability onto local administrative units and compelled them to cut costs and justify expenditure through measurable outcomes. In effect, socialist institutions—cultural included—were reconstituted as semi-autonomous enterprises whose legitimacy depended on financial performance as much as on criteria such as ideological conformity or aesthetic value.
zh: 在这一更广泛的经济转向中，自筹经费体制成为使紧缩正当化、同时提高财政汲取能力的关键工具。其设计意在使机构对自身预算承担部分责任，将经济可持续性的负担转移给地方行政单位，迫使它们削减成本，并通过可衡量的结果来证明支出的合理性。实际上，包括文化机构在内的社会主义机构被重构为半自主的企业，其正当性既依赖意识形态上的符合要求或审美价值等标准，也依赖财务绩效。

en: However, despite its ubiquity as a governing principle across the economy, self-financing acquired a distinct and uneven articulation in the cultural sector. Official discourse simultaneously reaffirmed culture as ideologically essential to socialist life and framed it as a domain of “limited resources” that required “prudence and rational allocation.”

In institutional terms, this tension was translated into stringent budgetary controls that turned cultural organizations into laboratories for experimenting with economic discipline under conditions of scarcity. This reorientation is visible in state budgetary allocations. While agricultural funding rose by as much as 9 percent, cultural budgets were sharply reduced by 47 percent, falling from 1.16 billion lei in 1983 to 735.2 million in 1984.

Although the 1986 budget appeared to signal recovery, with culture rising to 2.7 billion lei, it remained marginal relative to other sectors (education received 22 billion lei; social security 45 billion). More decisive than overall levels, however, was the restructuring of funding itself: only 23 percent of cultural expenditure was covered by the state (620 million lei), while the remaining 77 percent had to be generated autonomously by cultural institutions themselves.

On the one hand, this inversion reflected the withdrawal of institutional safety nets and the shifting of financial responsibility onto cultural institutions. On the other, it laid the ideological and operational foundations for the entrenchment of self-financing into everyday practice, which effectively bound institutional survival to income generation.
zh: 然而，尽管自筹经费作为治理原则遍及整个经济，它在文化部门却获得了独特而不均衡的表达。官方话语一方面重申文化对社会主义生活具有不可或缺的意识形态意义，另一方面又把文化描述为一个‘资源有限’、需要‘审慎和合理配置’的领域。
在制度层面，这种张力被转化为严格的预算控制，使文化组织成为在稀缺条件下试验经济纪律的实验室。国家预算分配清晰体现了这一转向：农业经费增加幅度高达9%，文化预算却大幅削减47%，从1983年的11.6亿列伊下降到1984年的7.352亿列伊。
尽管1986年文化预算增至27亿列伊，似乎预示复苏，相对于其他部门它仍属边缘：教育获得220亿列伊，社会保障获得450亿。比总额更具决定性的，是经费结构本身的重组：国家仅承担文化支出的23%，即6.2亿列伊，其余77%必须由文化机构自主创收。
一方面，这种倒转反映出机构保障网的撤回以及财务责任向文化机构的转移；另一方面，它为自筹经费扎根于日常实践奠定了意识形态和操作层面的基础，实际上将机构生存与收入创造绑定起来。

en: The asymmetry of this implementation was exacerbated by a recurrent tension in official discourse, which oscillated between regarding culture as structurally “non-productive” and potentially “wasteful,” associated with “excessive expenditure”

relative to measurable output, and simultaneously affirming its latent economic value as a domain that could be made more efficient and self-sustaining. Both public rhetoric and internal administrative reports—preserved in official bulletins and confidential documentation—mobilized this ambiguity to frame cultural spending as a site requiring optimization. In this way, rather than resolving the contradiction between cultural value and economic inefficiency, the regime rendered it productive as a justification for austerity measures in the sector. Claims of presumed extravagance—although archival records do not confirm the extent of such excess—thus persisted as a distortion to be corrected, in which culture remained singled out as a sphere in need of reform.
zh: 这种实施上的不对称，又被官方话语中反复出现的张力加剧：官方一时把文化看作结构上‘非生产性’且可能‘浪费’的领域，认为相对于可衡量的产出，它伴随着‘过度支出’；

同时又肯定其潜在经济价值，认为它可以变得更高效、更能自我维持。保存在官方简报和机密文件中的公共言论及内部行政报告，都利用这种含混，将文化支出塑造成需要优化的对象。这样，体制并未解决文化价值与经济低效之间的矛盾，而是让这一矛盾发挥作用，为文化部门的紧缩措施提供正当理由。于是，对所谓奢费的指责——虽然档案并未证实这种过度开支究竟有多普遍——持续把它呈现为需要纠正的失真，而文化始终被特别标记为一个需要改革的领域。

en: As early as 1981, Teodor Iovănescu—an economist who wrote and advised extensively on the introduction of self-financing in the cultural sector—warned of this necessity in times of crisis. In his report on the “optimization of cultural activity,” the state would aim to reduce central allocations while concurrently producing the necessary conditions for a transition “as urgently as possible, to a system of full self-financing.”

Iovănescu framed this shift as a structural reconfiguration in which the very existence of cultural institutions would soon be tied to their economic performance. This followed the directives of Ceaușescu himself, who, one year prior, in 1980, called for a rapid restructuring of the cultural sector. In his words:
zh: 早在1981年，曾广泛撰文并就文化部门引入自筹经费提供咨询的经济学家特奥多尔·约沃内斯库，就警告说危机时期有这种必要。他在关于‘优化文化活动’的报告中提出，国家应以减少中央拨款为目标，同时创造必要条件，‘尽可能紧急地’转向‘完全自筹经费的制度’。
约沃内斯库将这一转变描述为结构性重组，文化机构是否能够存在，很快就将与其经济绩效挂钩。这遵循了齐奥塞斯库本人的指示：早在前一年即1980年，他就要求迅速重组文化部门。他说：

en: It is necessary that, in a short time, we base the entire activity on principles of self-management [
] and self-governance [

]. […] Each theater, cultural center, house of culture must have its own budget of revenues and expenditures, must know how much it can spend, and also what it must provide. Just as a worker works eight hours, those in social and cultural activities must know that they are required to work a certain number of hours and accomplish specific activities. This is also true for music, where we have a number of ensembles that must present to the working people a set number of concert hours per week. Everything can and must be organized according to the principles of self-management. (
zh: 我们必须在短时间内，把全部活动建立在自我管理[
]和自我治理[
]的原则之上。[…]每一家剧院、文化中心、文化宫都必须有自己的收支预算，必须知道自己能花多少钱，也必须知道自己要提供什么。正如工人每天工作八小时一样，从事社会和文化活动的人必须知道，他们需要工作一定的时数，并完成特定活动。音乐也是如此：我们有一些团体，必须每周向劳动人民提供规定时数的音乐会。一切都可以、也必须按照自我管理的原则来组织。（

en: Nevertheless, the reform did not unfold overnight. Despite calls for “urgency,” the shift materialized incrementally as the product of cumulative policy layering that had piled up across nearly two decades. With the aim of curbing cultural expenditure and disciplining the sector, it fulfilled a long-standing ideological trajectory of legislation stretching back as far as 1971.
New self-financing logics were implanted onto existing structures, culminating in
(1985), which mandated that virtually all (cultural) institutions assume some degree of self-reliance, albeit to uneven and institutionally differentiated extents.
zh: 然而，改革并非一夜之间展开。尽管不断呼吁‘紧迫性’，转变仍是渐进形成的，是近二十年间政策层层累积的结果。为了抑制文化支出并约束这一部门，它落实了一条至少可追溯至1971年的长期立法意识形态轨迹。
新的自筹经费逻辑被植入既有结构，最终形成1985年的
，要求几乎所有文化机构在一定程度上自立，只是程度不一，并依机构而有差别。

en: The most visible effects of this layering of cultural policy were the imposition of economic targets and new expectations of output. With the exception of cinemas, theaters, and music institutions—which already quantified premieres and spectators—most cultural organizations entered the 1980s without predefined economic performance indicators. Gradually, however, official discourse acknowledged that cultural-artistic units required differentiated forms of evaluation and financing. By the late 1980s, the self-financing model had coagulated into a fully articulated system, complete with explicit economic targets and genre-specific benchmarks that reconditioned the operational logic of cultural institutions. Professional music institutions (operas, philharmonics, orchestras) saw their self-financing targets rise from 20 percent in 1981 to 75 percent in 1985 and 79 percent by 1988.
From 1985, houses of culture
) were required to achieve full (100 percent) self-financing, up from 85 percent in 1984. Local cultural centers (
) and folk art schools (
) both transitioned to full self-financing in 1984.
zh: 这种文化政策层层叠加最明显的效果，是强加经济指标和新的产出预期。除电影院、剧院和音乐机构原本已对首演及观众数量进行量化之外，大多数文化组织进入1980年代时，都没有预先规定的经济绩效指标。但官方话语逐渐承认，文化艺术单位需要不同形式的评估和经费安排。到1980年代后期，自筹经费模式已凝结为一套充分成形的体系，配有明确的经济目标和针对不同门类的基准，重新塑造了文化机构的运作逻辑。专业音乐机构，包括歌剧院、爱乐乐团和管弦乐团，其经费自筹目标从1981年的20%上升至1985年的75%，并在1988年达到79%。
文化宫（
）从1985年起被要求实现完全即100%自筹，比1984年的85%进一步提高。地方文化中心（
）和民间艺术学校（
）则都在1984年转为全额自筹。

en: Such targets were far from arbitrary and reflected entrenched cultural hierarchies that structured internal differentiation within the cultural field. Self-financing did not operate uniformly across cultural production but generated a graded system of expectations in which cultural genres and institutions were evaluated according to their perceived commercial potential, thereby transforming hierarchy into an operational principle of economic governance that distinguished institutions with greater revenue prospects from those deemed less profitable. Underlying this distinction was, in Iovănescu’s view, the idea that social recognition was increasingly contingent on institutional form, insofar as an organization’s capacity to survive independently of state subsidies was determined by its commercial viability.

To be more precise, for commodifiable cultural outputs (Iovănescu mentions books, visual art, music records, and live performances), value was to be mediated by the possibility of market exchange: sales and revenues translated cultural effort into measurable output, while unsold inventories or withdrawn performances signaled limited societal recognition and required producers to adjust output to perceived consumer demand.
zh: 这些目标绝非任意设定，而是反映了根深蒂固、塑造文化场域内部分化的文化等级。自筹经费并未在文化生产中一律运行，而是形成一套分等级的预期体系，按照被认为具有的商业潜力评价文化门类和机构。因此，等级被转化为经济治理的操作原则，把创收前景较好的机构同被认为较难盈利的机构区分开来。在约沃内斯库看来，这一区分背后的理念是，社会认可日益取决于机构形式，因为一个组织能否脱离国家补贴而生存，取决于其商业可行性。
更准确地说，对于可商品化的文化产出——约沃内斯库提及图书、视觉艺术、音乐唱片和现场演出——价值须经由市场交换的可能性来中介：销售额和收入将文化努力转化为可衡量的产出，未售出的库存或撤下的演出则表明社会认可有限，要求生产者按照其所感知的消费者需求调整产出。

en: In practice, this demand subjected institutions to a form of quasi-market discipline, as they started being evaluated through consumption patterns and sales performance. Put differently, institutions were expected to recalibrate both administrative operations and cultural-curatorial programming to austerity conditions; they had to learn to anticipate and respond to demand signals as if operating according to market relations and under supply-and-demand mechanisms. Yet the expectation of economic self-reliance and market-like conduct unfolded without many of the institutional conditions associated with market coordination. As a result, while the reforms did not create market relations in any straightforward sense, they did expand the role of economic evaluation in a centrally administered system and compelled actors to pursue revenue and develop market sensibilities. This category included entities with legal personality and the commercial potential to sustain themselves: the main film studios (“București,” “Alexandru Sahia,” “Animafilm”), the Romanian Radio and Television Network, and the “Romaniafilm” distribution company. Likewise, fully self-financing institutions included commercial powerhouses like publishing houses and daily newspapers, and ARIA (Romanian Artistic Booking Agency). Partially self-financing institutions, such as theaters and philharmonics, covered their remaining expenses through allocations from local supervisory authorities or central state budgets.
zh: 在实践中，这一要求使机构接受某种准市场纪律，因为它们开始依据消费模式和销售表现受到评价。换言之，机构被要求按照紧缩条件重新调整行政运作以及文化和策展安排；它们必须学会预判并回应需求信号，仿佛是在市场关系和供求机制下运行。然而，对经济自立和类似市场行为的要求，却是在缺少许多市场协调所需制度条件的情况下展开的。因此，改革虽未直接创造出市场关系，却扩大了经济评估在中央管理体制中的作用，迫使行动者追求收入并培养市场敏感性。这一类别包括具有法人资格和商业自立潜力的实体：主要电影制片厂‘București’、‘Alexandru Sahia’和‘Animafilm’，罗马尼亚广播电视网络，以及‘Romaniafilm’发行公司。同样，完全自筹经费的机构还包括出版社、日报社等商业实力较强的单位，以及ARIA，即罗马尼亚艺术演出经纪机构。剧院和爱乐乐团等部分自筹的机构，则由地方主管部门拨款或中央国家预算承担其余费用。

en: The episode highlighted at the start of this article, when Ceaușescu insisted that cinema must financially sustain itself, foreshadowed this broader reconfiguration of culture. More than a mere signal of intent, it articulated a proto-market paradigm in which cultural value was measured through commercial success and quantifiable income. By requiring cultural institutions to fund their own operations, the regime destabilized the traditional autonomy of the cultural field and subjected it to the heteronomous logic of economic rationality. Rather than a simple displacement of socialist principles for capitalist ones, the result was the coexistence of two partially overlapping and often contradictory logics: one promising disinterested symbolic production for the socialist polity, the other demanding profitability and measurable returns—a friction that reconfigured both everyday institutional practice and the meaning of culture itself. In the next paragraphs I explore how this logic was refracted in practice, where it took distinct forms across institutional typologies.
zh: 本文开头所述齐奥塞斯库坚持要求电影业在财务上自我维持的插曲，预示了文化领域这一更广泛的重组。它不仅仅表达意向，还阐明了一种原初市场范式，以商业成功和可量化收入衡量文化价值。通过要求文化机构自行承担运营经费，体制动摇了文化场域传统的自主性，使它服从经济理性这一他律逻辑。结果并非资本主义原则简单取代社会主义原则，而是两套部分重叠、经常相互矛盾的逻辑共存：一套承诺为社会主义政治共同体开展不以私利为目的的象征生产，另一套则要求盈利和可衡量的回报。这种摩擦既重组了机构日常实践，也重塑了文化本身的意义。接下来的几段将探讨这一逻辑如何在实践中被折射，并在不同类型的机构中采取独特形式。

en: For instance, in 1984, theaters and music institutions were explicitly told to “amplify and diversify activities,” increase revenues, and reduce expenditures. Rationalization translated into contraction and creative labor was subordinated to economic discipline to the extent that, between 1980 and 1987, personnel reductions reached up to 52 percent in certain arts and culture sectors, while music institutions alone accounted for a reduction of 1,660 staff positions.

Yet most institutions still failed to meet financial targets, and some, like Ungureanu’s Opera, struggled to pay salaries. At the same time, output surged: 25,814 performances (7,500 more than the previous year), 234 premieres (a 42 percent increase), and a 22 percent growth in audiences.

This contradiction reveals another paradox of late-socialist governance: survival relied on measurable output, yet austerity did not suppress cultural production. At least from the vantage point of the archival record—which is partial and itself performs state narratives—artistic activity appears to have intensified, as cultural production was increasingly organized through economic indicators of growth that expanded the operational scope of a cultural market in the making. In this context, output indicators came to function as proxies for economic performance and ideological vitality, and institutional legitimacy was conflated with both.
zh: 例如，1984年，剧院和音乐机构被明确要求‘扩大并丰富活动’，增加收入、减少支出。合理化落实为收缩，创造性劳动服从于经济纪律，以至于1980年至1987年，某些艺术文化部门的人员缩减幅度高达52%，仅音乐机构就减少了1,660个岗位。
然而，大多数机构仍未能达到财务目标，有些机构，例如温古雷亚努的歌剧院，甚至难以支付工资。与此同时，产出激增：演出25,814场，比前一年多7,500场；首演234部，增长42%；观众增加22%。
这一矛盾揭示了社会主义晚期治理的另一悖论：生存依赖可衡量的产出，但紧缩并未压制文化生产。至少从档案记录的角度看——这些记录是局部的，且本身也在展演国家叙事——艺术活动似乎有所强化，因为文化生产日益依照经济增长指标来组织，扩大了一个正在形成的文化市场的运作范围。在此情境下，产出指标开始充当经济绩效和意识形态活力的替代尺度，机构正当性则与二者混为一谈。

en: Notably, not all institutions were equally exposed to this logic, since the cultural sector was restratified along lines of institutional typology and perceived commercial potential. Certain public-service institutions (such as libraries or museums) were sheltered from the self-financing architecture. In contrast with the previous institutional categorization, the social value of the labor of these institutions (and their corresponding degree of insulation from exposure to economic discipline) was determined less by price than by broader civic functions. The services they offered were generally free of charge, and while not entirely exempt from self-financing requirements, such establishments faced lower thresholds and reduced economic expectations. For example, in 1985, museums were only expected to self-finance 39 percent of their activity. Despite some growth, by 1988, the rate had only reached 55 percent.
zh: 值得注意的是，并非所有机构都同等暴露在这套逻辑之下，因为文化部门按机构类型及被认为具有的商业潜力重新分层。某些公共服务机构，例如图书馆或博物馆，受到保护，免于全面进入自筹经费架构。与前一类机构不同，这些机构劳动的社会价值，以及相应地免受经济纪律约束的程度，较少由价格决定，更多由广泛的公共职能决定。它们提供的服务通常免费；虽然并非完全豁免自筹要求，这类机构面对的门槛和经济预期都较低。例如，1985年博物馆只被要求自行筹措其活动经费的39%；此后虽有所增加，到1988年该比例也仅达55%。

en: Ultimately, although differentiated, late-socialist reforms integrated parameters of austerity and economic rationalization into the very language of cultural governance. While the broader self-financing regime marked a profound shift in the sector,

(1985) was its decisive turning point. With it, financing ceased to be an administrative detail and became a governing principle of cultural life. It shaped budgets, institutional priorities, and the logic of cultural production itself. By introducing explicit economic targets and performance benchmarks, the law institutionalized a mode of evaluation oriented less around ideological fulfillment alone and more around metrics of revenue generation and measurable institutional outcomes.
zh: 归根结底，虽然实行差异化安排，社会主义晚期的改革仍把紧缩和经济合理化的参数融入文化治理的语言本身。更广泛的自筹经费体制标志着该部门的深刻转变，而1985年
则是其决定性的转折点。随着这部法律出台，经费不再是行政细节，而成为文化生活的治理原则。它塑造预算、机构优先事项以及文化生产自身的逻辑。该法引入明确的经济目标和绩效基准，使一种评价方式制度化：其取向不再仅仅围绕意识形态目标的实现，而更多围绕创收指标及可衡量的机构成果。

en: In doing so, it codified sectoral distinctions, sharpened existing hierarchies, and—despite its gradual rollout—pushed cultural institutions and actors into a high-stakes process of continuous adaptation. This differentiation points in two directions. On the one hand, it suggests that socialist authorities resisted a uniform model and instead calibrated expectations according to institutional function and perceived economic potential, which also indicates an awareness of the tensions embedded in the policy design. On the other hand, it is precisely in this asymmetry that the politics of evaluation becomes visible: state socialism sought to preserve a hierarchical cultural order while simultaneously engineering new forms of economic viability within the same institutional field. In this way, differentiation became a stratifying mechanism that (re)produced hierarchies and their own uneven distribution of risk and responsibility.
zh: 如此一来，法律将部门差别法定化，加深既有等级，而且尽管实施渐进，仍把文化机构及行动者推入一个利害攸关的持续适应过程。这种差异化指向两个方面。一方面，它表明社会主义当局并不接受统一模式，而是按机构功能和预期经济潜力调整要求，这也说明它们意识到政策设计内含的张力。另一方面，恰恰在这种不对称中，评价的政治性变得可见：国家社会主义试图维持一个等级化的文化秩序，同时又在同一制度场域内设计新的经济生存形式。如此，差异化就成为一种分层机制，生产并再生产各种等级，以及风险和责任的不均衡分配。

en: In addition to imposing new economic expectations, the self-financing regime reshaped the subjectivities of cultural directors and artists, who were compelled to internalize managerial rationalities and fiscal discipline. As the next section shows, whether individuals navigated these pressures skillfully or struggled to keep pace, all were forced to adapt or risk marginalization. The result was a patchwork of institutional strategies, one that reveals how unevenly top-down mandates were translated into the daily realities of cultural work.
zh: 自筹经费体制除了施加新的经济预期，也重塑文化主管和艺术家的主体性，迫使他们将管理理性和财政纪律内化。下一节将表明，无论个人能够熟练应对这些压力，还是难以跟上，所有人都被迫适应，否则就有被边缘化的风险。其结果是形形色色的机构策略，而这些策略揭示了自上而下的要求如何不均衡地转化为文化工作的日常现实。

en: Entrepreneurialism without Capitalism: Cultural Labor and The Path to the “First Million”
zh: 没有资本主义的企业家精神：文化劳动与通往‘第一个百万’之路

en: The pressures of late-socialist economic reform compelled cultural workers to adopt forms of entrepreneurialism that redefined artistic labor and professional security. For instance, music pedagogues—once a protected group of conservatory-trained specialists—now had to attract fee-paying students to secure their positions or risk dismissal. Previously subsidized with 5 million lei annually, Bucharest’s

was required to meet a 95 percent self-financing target and was consequently forced to reduce its staff (to sixty-one teachers, forty-one of them on half-time) and raise tuition fees. While a total of 1,399 fee-paying pupils secured the institution’s future, a minimum of twelve such students justified a single half-time teaching post. In effect, the burden of institutional survival was displaced onto individual teaching staff, who were required to secure enrollments as a condition of maintaining employment. Among the casualties of this reorganization was internationally celebrated cellist and prize-winning composer Şerban Nichifor, who was dismissed and permitted to return only on the condition that he personally “recruit the required dozen students.”
zh: 社会主义晚期经济改革的压力，迫使文化工作者采取各种企业家式做法，重新界定艺术劳动与职业保障。例如，音乐教师原本是受保护、经音乐学院训练的专门人才，如今必须吸引付费学生来保住职位，否则就可能被解雇。布加勒斯特

原先每年获得500万列伊补贴，此时却被要求达到95%的经费自筹目标，因此被迫裁减人员，只留下61位教师，其中41位为半职，同时提高学费。总共1,399名付费学生保障了机构的未来，而至少12名这样的学生才足以支持一个半职教师岗位。事实上，机构生存的负担被转移到每位教师身上，他们必须保证招生数量，才能继续就业。国际知名大提琴家、获奖作曲家谢尔班·尼基福尔也是这场重组的受损者之一：他被解雇，只有在亲自‘招到所要求的12名学生’的条件下才获准回任。

en: If we can speak of a “Nichifor case,” it exemplifies how the late-socialist turn to self-financing generated a new evaluative grammar that blurred the line between cultural status and economic performance, and exacerbated preexisting forms of precarity. Under these conditions, initiative itself became a dominant mode of institutional survival. The same archival report further indicates that amateur music instructors—often more agile in recruiting students—gained an advantage over credentialed professionals, who had to balance teaching hours with the artistic duties of rehearsing, auditioning, performing, and composing that had secured their institutional standing in the first place.

While this shift could be read as a democratization of access to formerly prestigious teaching positions, it also reveals how criteria of cultural authority and cultural labor more broadly were redefined under the strains of a quasi-market environment.
zh: 如果可以称之为‘尼基福尔事件’，那么它体现了社会主义晚期转向自筹经费如何产生一种新的评价语法，模糊文化地位与经济绩效的界线，并加剧既有的不稳定处境。在这些条件下，主动谋划本身成为机构生存的一种主导方式。同一份档案报告进一步表明，业余音乐教师通常招生更灵活，因此比拥有正式资质的专业人士更具优势；后者不得不在教学时数与排练、试演、演出、作曲等艺术职责之间取得平衡，而恰恰是这些职责最初奠定了他们的机构地位。
虽然这种转变可以被解读为让原本享有声望的教学职位向更多人开放、实现民主化，但它也揭示了准市场环境的压力如何重新界定文化权威，以及更广泛意义上文化劳动的评价标准。

en: A similar dynamic is evident in the case of Ungureanu, director of the Craiova Opera, where institutional survival became contingent on entrepreneurial ingenuity and ad hoc revenue-generating initiatives. His successor set up a small video library with two televisions screening up to six VHS films a day for modest entry fees—a semi-legal arrangement tolerated insofar as it kept the opera afloat financially.

Such adaptations show how, under measures of austerity, the prestige of high-art institutions was refracted through economic rationality; at the same time, they reveal a fragile choreography of necessity in which artistic legitimacy was renegotiated through revenue-making practices. In the shadow of late socialism’s pervasive contradictions, two interrelated transformations become visible: first, institutional evaluation shifted, with prestige and formal credentials gradually ceding ground to market responsiveness as the dominant criterion of success. Second, cultural labor became increasingly mediated by quantifiable metrics of self-financing (e.g., number of pupils, tuition revenues, income targets). As professional legitimacy was made conditional on economic performance, it may also be that institutional success came to rest less on
quotas were achieved than on the fact that they were achieved at all, however precariously or inventively they were met.
zh: 克拉约瓦歌剧院院长温古雷亚努的案例也显示出类似动态：机构生存开始取决于企业家式机智以及临时创收举措。他的继任者建了一个小型录像放映室，用两台电视每天最多播放六部VHS影片，收取少量门票。这是一种半合法的安排，只要它能在财务上维持歌剧院，便得到容忍。

这类适应显示，在紧缩措施下，高雅艺术机构的声望如何经经济理性而折射；与此同时，它们也揭示了一套出于生存需要而进行的脆弱协调，艺术正当性在其中通过创收实践被重新协商。在社会主义晚期普遍矛盾的阴影下，可以看到两项相互关联的转变：首先，机构评价发生变化，声望和正式资格逐渐让位于市场回应能力，后者成为主导性的成功标准。其次，文化劳动日益通过可量化的自筹经费指标来中介，例如学生人数、学费收入和收入目标。当职业正当性以经济绩效为条件时，机构成功或许也越来越不取决于指标
完成，而只取决于指标是否确实完成，无论完成方式多么岌岌可危或富于巧思。

en: Beyond moments of turmoil, the archive registers a vivid atmosphere of entrepreneurial euphoria. News reports capture the translation of a seemingly unsettled moment into an episode of effervescence. Suddenly tasked with transforming cultural activity into revenue, the cultural directors of the 1980s proudly showcased their recipe for entrepreneurial success and their paths to the “first million.” At the Municipal Cultural House Brașov, for example, the 1984 shift to 85 percent self-financing yielded a 209,000 lei surplus, and by October 1985 revenues had reached 1.31 million lei against a 1.05 million lei plan.
A similar account from 1987, published in the party newspaper
, saw the director of the Trade Union Cultural House in Târgu Jiu, Mihai Rață, proudly announce, “We’ve hit the million.”

The same celebratory tone is evident in Florica Șerbănescu’s report, the chief cultural official for Galați County. There, in the first quarter of 1984, cultural institutions generated four times more revenue than the previous year, and as a result of new measures, self-financing theaters and music institutions were projected to raise their annual income by an additional two million lei.
zh: 除了动荡时刻，档案也记录了一种鲜活的企业家式亢奋氛围。新闻报道呈现了一个看似不安定的时刻如何转变为充满热情的片段。1980年代的文化主管突然肩负将文化活动转化为收入的任务，却骄傲地展示企业经营成功的秘诀，以及通向‘第一个百万’的道路。例如，布拉索夫市文化宫在1984年转为85%自筹后，产生20.9万列伊盈余；到1985年10月，收入已达到131万列伊，超过105万列伊的计划。
1987年党报
的一篇类似报道中，特尔古日乌工会文化宫主任米哈伊·拉策自豪地宣布：‘我们达到百万了。’
加拉茨县文化主管弗洛里卡·谢尔伯内斯库的报告也体现出同样的庆祝语调。1984年第一季度，当地文化机构的创收达到前一年的四倍；实施新措施后，自筹经费的剧院和音乐机构预计还将把年收入再提高200万列伊。

en: Echoing the mythic productivity of socialist workers, cultural actors were now nudged toward a different, almost tongue-in-cheek horizon of aspiration: the seductive grammar of “hitting the first million.” In this seemingly paradoxical configuration, cultural institutions were simultaneously disciplined by logics of planned productivity and lured by market benchmarks of success, which revealed how ideological and economic performances collided yet remained mutually constitutive. Several key strategies of commodification can be noticed in their attempt to meet quotas: in Brașov, alongside strict cost-saving measures such as cutting electricity by 57 percent, expansion was centered on monetizing cultural knowledge and skills through fee-paying courses (including technical drawing, folk dance, photography, and apiculture) that attracted up to 1,100 participants.

Rață’s success in Târgu Jiu relied on the commodification of cultural participation and entertainment through large-scale programming: its offerings ranged from live music and theater performances to cine-club screenings and public debates. Approximately 600 events were reported annually, attracting nearly 800,000 attendees, 20 percent of whom were active participants.
zh: 呼应着社会主义工人神话般的生产力，文化行动者此时被推向另一种几乎带着戏谑意味的志向：‘赚到第一个百万’这一诱人的表达。在这种看似矛盾的配置中，文化机构既受到计划生产逻辑的约束，又被市场成功的标杆吸引，揭示意识形态表现与经济绩效如何相互冲撞，却仍彼此构成。从它们完成指标的努力中，可以看到几项关键的商品化策略：在布拉索夫，除节电57%等严格节约措施外，业务扩张主要通过收费课程把文化知识与技能变现。课程包括技术制图、民间舞蹈、摄影和养蜂，吸引了多达1,100名参与者。
拉策在特尔古日乌的成功，则依赖大规模活动安排，把文化参与和娱乐商品化：内容从现场音乐、戏剧演出，到电影俱乐部放映和公开讨论。据报道，每年约有600场活动，吸引近80万人次，其中20%为积极参与者。

en: In the case of Șerbănescu’s Galați County, an alternative strategy can be noticed. Live performance institutions, such as theaters and philharmonics, were instructed to double their shows—from 1,086 in 1983 to 2,190 in 1984—and maintain attendance rates of up to 95 percent.

Keeping such high attendance was no easy feat, so cultural authorities were concerned with retaining established audiences while also attracting new ones. Maintaining established audiences involved transforming attendance into a reliable source of revenue, and institutions introduced monthly subscriptions as a means to monetize loyalty. To attract new audiences, orchestras and theater troupes extended their mobility across the county, performing beyond urban centers in factories, staging open-air shows in parks and stadiums, and offering educational programs. This multifaceted strategy shows how cultural production was reconfigured to meet both financial and ideological-pedagogical imperatives. Most strikingly, institutions whose legitimacy was grounded in artistic creation marketed their own staff’s labor commercially. In doing so, they offered carpentry, tailoring, or interior-decorating services to the general public in a clear recoding of cultural labor as marketable craftsmanship.
zh: 在谢尔伯内斯库所在的加拉茨县，还能看到另一种策略。剧院、爱乐乐团等现场演出机构被要求把场次增加一倍，从1983年的1,086场增至1984年的2,190场，并保持高达95%的上座率。

维持如此高的上座率并非易事，因此文化主管部门既关心留住既有观众，也关心吸引新观众。留住既有观众意味着把观看演出转化为可靠收入，机构推出月票，以此把忠诚度变现。为吸引新观众，管弦乐团和剧团扩大在县内的流动范围，走出城市中心到工厂演出，在公园和体育场举行露天表演，并提供教育项目。这种多面策略显示，文化生产如何被重组，以同时满足财务和意识形态教育的要求。最引人注目的是，那些以艺术创作为正当性基础的机构，开始在商业上销售自身员工的劳动。它们向公众提供木工、裁缝或室内装饰服务，明确将文化劳动重新编码为可出售的手艺。

en: According to the archival record, the measures appear to have worked, and this reworked “perform or perish” logic precipitated a distinct form of “socialist entrepreneurialism.” Authorities celebrated financial achievements as proof that culture could, quite literally, pay for itself, and more. Entrepreneurial behavior, when aligned with broader political objectives, was recast as a distinct socialist virtue. Cultural revenues were paraded as the regime’s success, and austerity itself was rebranded as triumph: in 1988 alone, at the peak of the self-financing regime, the nationwide 145 professional theater and music institutions staged nearly 47,000 performances for over 18 million spectators, up from 38,000 shows and 16 million attendees in 1983.

Such soaring figures were not incidental but symptomatic of a radically redesigned cultural sector, in which institutions operated as productive enterprises and success was defined through the conversion of artistic production into quantified output and indicators of accelerated growth. The celebrated goal of “hitting the million” functioned as both an imposed economic target and a prized symbol of managerial competence. In consequence, financial performance was naturalized as the proxy for professional accomplishment. Culture was instrumentalized as the means, financial success the end.
zh: 据档案记录，这些措施似乎奏效，而经过改写的‘表演否则灭亡’逻辑，催生了一种独特的‘社会主义企业家精神’。当局赞颂财务成果，以此证明文化确实能够支付自身成本，甚至有余。当企业家式行为与更广泛的政治目标一致时，它就被重塑为一种独特的社会主义美德。文化收入被拿来展示体制的成功，紧缩本身也被重新包装为胜利：仅在自筹经费体制达到顶点的1988年，全国145家专业戏剧和音乐机构就为逾1,800万人次观众演出了近47,000场，高于1983年的38,000场和1,600万人次。
如此飙升的数字并非偶然，而是文化部门被根本性重构的表现：机构像生产企业一样运作，成功则通过把艺术生产转化为量化产出和加速增长指标来定义。受到赞颂的‘达到百万’目标，既是被施加的经济指标，也是备受推崇的管理能力象征。于是，财务绩效被自然化为职业成就的替代尺度。文化被工具化为手段，财务成功则成为目的。

en: Yet this impressive output masked deeper disillusionment, as cultural actors remained estranged from the financial rewards their labor generated. Ungureanu, director of Opera Craiova, recalled working tirelessly “for the institution to earn some money,” only to discover that the 475-lei bonus he had received (after a twenty-five-lei tax deduction) was a mistake; the payment was meant for a printing press technician who shared his name.

Rather than a merely tragicomic episode, the incident illustrates the unstable moral economy of a system in which cultural labor was rapidly redefined through managerial and financial categories, and where “entrepreneurialism” emerged not as market freedom but as a state-imposed obligation to sustain institutional solvency.
zh: 然而，这些令人瞩目的产出掩盖了更深的幻灭，因为文化行动者仍然无法享有自身劳动创造的财务回报。克拉约瓦歌剧院院长温古雷亚努回忆，他不知疲倦地工作，‘让机构挣点钱’，后来却发现自己收到的475列伊奖金——已扣除25列伊税款——竟是一次误付；这笔钱本该付给一位与他同名的印刷厂技术员。
这一事件不只是悲喜交加的插曲，还说明了某种不稳定的道德经济：在这个体制中，文化劳动迅速被管理和财务范畴重新界定，‘企业家精神’并非作为市场自由出现，而是作为国家强加的、维持机构偿付能力的义务出现。

en: Across institutions, this reconfiguration translated into intensified labor regimes in which success depended on the compression of time and the multiplication of output. As recalled by Alexandru Racu, choir master of the Oltenia Philharmonic (credited with over 350 premieres and more than 1,000 educational concerts), the self-financing years demanded “four or five lecture-concerts a day” and constant touring. “An exhausting effort,” he stated, “yet we survived.”

At the Târgu-Mureș National Theatre, director Iulius Moldovan similarly observed that during the 1986 season actors performed three to four shows daily, totaling approximately 3,200 activities each, to exceed revenue quotas and the planned audience target of 290,000 spectators. In Moldovan’s words, to match “this generous ambition, the theater is for an actor a permanent condition, a second life lived in multiple roles.”

Yet in addition to mere personal dedication, such recollections point to a systemic reliance on intensified labor: cultural production was sustained not through abundant resources, as authorities often lamented, but through the stretching of artistic work to meet revenue and output demands.
zh: 在各个机构中，这种重组转化为更高强度的劳动制度，成功取决于时间的压缩与产出的成倍增加。据奥尔特尼亚爱乐乐团合唱团指挥亚历山德鲁·拉库回忆——他曾参与逾350部作品首演及1,000多场教育音乐会——自筹经费的岁月要求‘每天四五场讲解音乐会’，并不停巡演。他说：‘累到筋疲力尽，但我们活下来了。’
特尔古穆列什国家剧院院长尤利乌斯·莫尔多万也指出，1986年演出季，演员每天演出三到四场，每人合计约3,200项活动，以超额完成收入指标及29万人次观众的计划目标。用莫尔多万的话说，为了匹配‘这一宏大的抱负，对演员而言，剧院是一种永久状态，是在多重角色中度过的第二人生’。
然而，这些回忆除了表明个人投入，还指向对劳动强化的系统性依赖：文化生产的维持并非靠充裕资源——当局常对资源不足表示遗憾——而是靠不断拉伸艺术劳动，以满足收入和产出的要求。

en: Beyond individualized experiences, cultural life in general was transformed into a race for revenue. As public subsidies declined and audience purchasing power remained arguably limited, institutions were drawn into new forms of resource competition: not a market competition among private actors but a struggle for financial viability within a socialist economy of scarcity. As Ungureanu later recalled, “We competed—Costin, Dincă, and I—over who among us directors could secure the largest contributions.”

What emerges is less a shift away from artistic excellence than a reconfiguration of institutional success, a struggle to maintain entrepreneurial stamina by demonstrating cultural production’s capacity to generate income in conditions of austerity. Freed from managerial duties, Ungureanu seemed relieved, since he could finally go back to music conducting and “minding [his] own business.”
zh: 超越个人经历，文化生活整体上都变成了一场收入竞赛。随着公共补贴减少、观众购买力大概仍有限，机构被卷入新形式的资源竞争：这不是私人行动者之间的市场竞争，而是在社会主义稀缺经济中争取财务生存。温古雷亚努后来回忆：‘我们在竞争——科斯廷、丁克和我——比谁这个院长能争取到最多的资助。’
这里发生的与其说是背离艺术卓越，不如说是重新界定机构成功：通过证明文化生产在紧缩条件下的创收能力，努力维持企业家式的耐力。摆脱管理职责后，温古雷亚努似乎如释重负，因为他终于可以重新从事音乐指挥，并‘管[自己]的事’。

en: The reorganization of work relations often spilled beyond institutional boundaries into everyday life. Under the austere climate of late socialism, individuals were encouraged to adopt forms of economic self-reliance not only within their workplaces—factories, offices, or cultural institutions—but also in domestic and community settings, where resourcefulness and network-building became practical necessities.
With an emphasis on social responsibility and local resource mobilization (
), households gradually came to be imagined and managed as miniature enterprises.

In this sense, practices associated with entrepreneurship under austerity can be read as a prelude to a longer, uneven entanglement of socialist governance with emergent market-oriented rationalities. Informal revenue-generating strategies, like charging for unofficial VHS screenings or bartering cultural goods for scarce consumer items,
illustrate how micro-level practices of economic improvisation permeated everyday cultural life prior to the formal consolidation of market institutions.
zh: 工作关系的重组常常越过机构边界，扩散到日常生活。在社会主义晚期的紧缩氛围中，个人不仅在工厂、办公室、文化机构等工作场所，也在家庭和社区环境中被鼓励实行经济自立；在那里，善于应变和建立关系网络成为实际必需。
随着社会责任和地方资源动员（
）得到强调，家庭逐渐被想象成微型企业，并按这一方式加以管理。
从这个意义上看，紧缩条件下与企业经营相关的实践，可以被理解为更漫长且不均衡的纠缠过程的序幕：社会主义治理与新兴市场取向理性在其中相互交织。非正式创收策略，例如对非官方VHS放映收费，或用文化产品交换短缺消费品，
显示出在市场制度正式巩固之前，经济应变的微观实践已渗透日常文化生活。

en: The rise of such practices also points to a deeper complexity, namely that the competencies associated with entrepreneurial conduct—and the language of enterprise—were neither fully cultivated nor formally legitimized as a normative ideal after four decades of socialism. Rather, the socialist system simultaneously constrained and enabled forms of economic improvisation that developed in tension with its ideological rejection of the market. As Martha Lampland has shown in her analysis of the commodification of labor in rural Hungary, late-socialist economies were organized around a structural tension that is often misread as ideological inconsistency but is better understood as constrained economic rationality: while villagers strongly endorsed socialist guarantees such as full employment, healthcare, and pensions, everyday life was organized around highly individualized strategies of economistic calculation and a sharp distinction between public provision and private survival. What appears as “capitalism-like” behavior—bootstrapping, utilitarianism, opportunistic exchange—was thus not external to socialism but generated within its institutional constraints, where scarcity and entitlement co-produced forms of market-oriented reasoning.

Katherine Verdery has further demonstrated that chronic shortages intensified these dynamics by pushing individuals toward an informal “second economy,” which—although not unique to socialism—meant that goods and services were secured through a vast repertoire of quasi-legal practices.
zh: 这些实践的兴起还指向更深一层的复杂性：经过四十年的社会主义，与企业家式行为相关的能力以及企业经营的语言，既未得到充分培育，也未作为规范性理想获得正式正当性。相反，社会主义体制同时限制并促成了各种经济应变形式，而这些形式的发展始终与其在意识形态上拒斥市场相冲突。玛莎·兰普兰在分析匈牙利农村劳动的商品化时指出，社会主义晚期经济围绕一种结构性张力组织起来。这种张力常被误读为意识形态不一致，但更适合被理解为受约束的经济理性：村民虽强烈支持充分就业、医疗和养老金等社会主义保障，日常生活却围绕高度个人化的经济计算策略，以及公共供给与私人求生之间的鲜明区分而展开。因此，看似‘类似资本主义’的行为——自力筹措、功利主义、机会主义交换——并非来自社会主义之外，而是产生于其制度约束之内：稀缺与应得权利共同生产了面向市场的推理方式。
凯瑟琳·韦尔德里进一步表明，长期短缺强化了这些动态，迫使个人转向非正式的‘第二经济’；虽然第二经济并非社会主义独有，但在这里，它意味着人们通过极为丰富的准合法实践获得商品与服务。

en: Elsewhere I have shown that such strategies extended deeply into the cultural field, where musicians often engaged in informal, sometimes illicit, practices while touring abroad. Members of the rock band
were charged with shoplifting in West Germany, Gheorghe Zamfir (later known for his contribution to the
soundtrack) sold music to West German porn producers, and musicians from
smuggled foreign currency in amplifiers and car parts while using fictitious Danish contracts to extend tours and evade taxation back home.
Documented by the

as moral deviance or anti-socialist behavior, these activities can be understood as situated strategies to compensate for domestic material scarcities and state management inefficiencies. From this perspective, the entrepreneurial repertoires of the 1980s did not emerge
but drew on preexisting, informal economies of adaptation, as previously clandestine practices were progressively absorbed into officially sanctioned forms of economic self-legitimation.
zh: 我在别处已经表明，这些策略深入文化场域，音乐家出国巡演时常常参与非正式、有时甚至非法的活动。摇滚乐队
的成员在西德被控入店行窃；格奥尔基·赞菲尔——后来因参与
配乐而为人所知——向西德色情影片制作人出售音乐；
乐队的音乐家则把外币藏在扩音器和汽车零件中走私，并利用虚构的丹麦合同延长巡演，逃避国内税收。
这些活动被
记录为道德越轨或反社会主义行为，但也可以理解为在特定情境下，补偿国内物质匮乏及国家管理低效的策略。从这一视角看，1980年代的企业家式行动方式并非
，而是利用了既有的非正式适应经济；原先秘密进行的实践，逐步被吸纳进官方认可的、通过经济表现证明自身正当性的形式中。

en: Amid contradictions and entanglements, not all cultural actors navigated this balancing act successfully. The archive, although never exhaustive, captures the uneven effects of institutional demands and preserves vivid evidence of failures as much as of successes. Several years before making his “first million,” Mihai Rață had drawn a sharp reprimand from socialist authorities for his passivity.

By 1987, he had evidently mastered the managerial craft, but at the decade’s outset, the same cultural institution he supervised stood at a precarious crossroads, struggling to meet the new demands. Five years earlier, open-house initiatives were held monthly rather than the recommended weekly, and authorities observed that “attempts at meaningful collaboration with enterprise-level trade unions remained tentative, and beyond the routine
nights, few initiatives had emerged.”

What happened subsequently was an arc embodying a socialist success story in entrepreneurialism. Nevertheless, if in Rață’s case public criticism appeared to act as a motivating force, in other instances, directors of underperforming institutions were required to undertake further staff development via retraining programs, which linked the expectations of meeting self-financing quotas directly to managerial capacity building.
zh: 在矛盾与纠缠之中，并非所有文化行动者都能成功保持这种平衡。档案虽从不穷尽一切，却捕捉到了机构要求所产生的不均衡效果，既鲜活地保存成功，也保存失败的证据。在赚到‘第一个百万’的几年前，米哈伊·拉策曾因消极不作为而受到社会主义当局严厉训斥。
到1987年，他显然已掌握管理技艺，但在这十年之初，由他主管的同一文化机构还处于岌岌可危的十字路口，难以满足新要求。五年前，开放活动不是按建议每周举行，而是每月一次；当局观察到，‘同企业级工会建立有意义合作的尝试仍停留在试探阶段，除了例行的
之夜，几乎没有新举措。’
此后发生的变化，构成了一则社会主义企业经营的成功故事。然而，如果说公开批评在拉策身上似乎起到了激励作用，那么在其他情况下，表现不佳机构的主管则被要求通过再培训项目接受进一步的人员培养，将完成自筹经费指标的要求直接与管理能力建设联系起来。

en: The following subsection examines the role of training programs in late socialism, showing how they sought to compensate for the absence of market-oriented skills and cultivate the performance-driven dispositions demanded by the self-financing regime.
zh: 下一小节考察培训项目在社会主义晚期的作用，说明这些项目如何试图弥补市场取向技能的缺失，并培养自筹经费体制所要求的绩效导向倾向。

en: From Apparatchik to Cultural Manager: Training Market-Oriented Conduct in Socialism
zh: 从党政干部到文化经理人：在社会主义中训练市场取向的行为

en: In a 1988 interview in

, Zenovia Niculescu—trainer of cultural directors and head of a cadre training center in Bucharest—signaled a consequential shift in cultural administration under the self-financing regime. The role of directors was being redefined through a “rational combination of professional knowledge with research and practice,” while new management methodologies oriented toward “economic-financial realization” were introduced alongside standard political-ideological guidance.

Yet this managerial retraining revealed a looming paradox: it sought to produce self-optimizing economic actors while simultaneously reaffirming their status as socialist functionaries bound by political-ideological loyalty. From this ambivalent process of reskilling emerged a hybrid figure that combined socialist rationalization with resource-driven technocratic logics and embodied a role previously absent from the socialist institutional landscape: the cultural manager.
zh: 1988年，文化主管培训者、布加勒斯特一所干部培训中心负责人泽诺维娅·尼古列斯库在
的一次访谈中，指出了自筹经费体制下文化行政的一项重大转变。主管的角色正通过‘将专业知识与研究、实践合理结合’而得到重新界定；在常规政治思想指导之外，也开始引入面向‘经济财务实现’的新管理方法。
然而，这种管理再培训暴露了一个日渐显现的悖论：它既试图造就自我优化的经济行动者，又重申他们是受政治思想忠诚约束的社会主义干部。从这种具有两面性的技能重塑中，出现了一个混合人物：他把社会主义合理化与资源驱动的技术官僚逻辑结合起来，体现出此前社会主义制度景观中不存在的角色，即文化经理人。

en: The imperative to “perfect” personnel ran as a red thread through documents of the late-socialist era and framed workforce improvement as central to social and professional mobility. The 13th Congress’s five-year plan (1986–1990) introduced directives for retraining and upskilling the national workforce, while projecting labor reorientations up to the year 2000. Targeting roughly three million people annually, the new statute emphasized renewing professional knowledge, acquiring additional qualifications to offset obsolescence, and mastering new methods in “scientific organization and the management of production.”

Building on these expansive retraining initiatives, Ceaușescu called for cadre “multi-development”—the fusion of technical-organizational competence with politico-ideological formation—reiterating the socialist ideal of the multilaterally developed individual.

In practice, this principle recast ideological dedication as insufficient without managerial efficiency. The need for hybridity was thus articulated from the highest party echelons. The “good activist” was both competent manager and ideological caretaker. Within this framework, the traditional cultural director—once primarily oriented toward artistic and curatorial judgment—saw their authority displaced; they risked being supplanted by a managerial type whose legitimacy was derived from the ability to balance artistic authority and ideological compliance with financial performance and self-sufficiency.
zh: ‘完善’人员的要求如一条红线贯穿社会主义晚期的文件，将劳动者素质提升置于社会和职业流动的核心。党的十三大五年计划（1986—1990年）提出对全国劳动者进行再培训和技能提升的指令，并将劳动力调整展望延伸至2000年。新规章每年以约300万人为对象，强调更新专业知识、取得额外资格以应对技能过时，以及掌握‘科学组织和生产管理’的新方法。
在这些广泛再培训举措的基础上，齐奥塞斯库呼吁干部‘多方面发展’，将技术组织能力同政治思想培养融合，重申社会主义关于个人全面发展的理想。
在实践中，这一原则意味着，缺少管理效率，仅有意识形态献身是不够的。对混合能力的需要，因而由党的最高层提出。‘优秀活动家’既是称职的管理者，也是意识形态的维护者。在此框架中，传统文化主管原本主要凭艺术和策展判断行事，其权威却遭到挤压；他们可能被一种管理型人物取代，后者的正当性来自在艺术权威、意识形态服从与财务绩效、自给自足之间取得平衡的能力。

en: To cultivate these dispositions, new regional training centers were established which, beyond artistic pedagogy and craft improvement, placed growing emphasis on economic and managerial literacy.

Niculescu described how the center under her coordination systematically adjusted its curricula to align cultural training with new political and economic imperatives, seeing these shifting aptitudes as “indispensable to the future.”
Her training model centered on the figure of the cultural administrator
(“attuned to the current state of affairs”), qualified to identify economic potential and manage resources efficiently through what she called
(“economic thinking”) intended to produce “positive effects in the optimization of cultural activity” in a “continuous state of learning.”
zh: 为培养这些倾向，新的地区培训中心相继建立，在艺术教学和技艺提高之外，日益强调经济与管理素养。
尼古列斯库描述了她所协调的中心如何系统调整课程，使文化培训符合新的政治经济要求，并将这些变化中的能力视为‘未来不可或缺’之物。
她的培训模式以一种文化管理者形象为中心：
，即‘紧跟当前事态’，具备识别经济潜力和高效管理资源的资格。他们通过她称为
的‘经济思维’，在‘持续学习状态’中对‘文化活动的优化产生积极影响’。

en: Training centers also oversaw the examination and certification of “freelance artists” (
organized courses for amateur artists willing to improve their craftsmanship,
and offered intensive crash courses to performers who showed promise at renowned pop music festivals like
(from diction to general music theory, and makeup to costume design).
In live performance specialization, for instance, participants in the 1986
program were not only immersed in rehearsals and artistic mentoring but trained in metrics of efficiency and audience research.

Across these training settings, artistic and ideological formation became increasingly subordinated to the logic of organizational performance, with economic and managerial competencies central to this reconfiguration. As a result, two “Ps”—“perfecting” (
) and “polyvalence” (
)—became defining idioms of cultural labor in the 1980s that echoed the socialist ideal of “multiskilling” (
) but now reoriented toward resourcefulness and self-management.
zh: 培训中心还负责‘自由职业艺术家’（
）的考试与认证，
为愿意提高技艺的业余艺术家组织课程，
并为在
等知名流行音乐节上显示潜力的表演者开设密集速成班，内容从吐字到一般乐理，从化妆到服装设计。
例如，在现场表演专业训练中，1986年
项目的参与者不仅投入排练、接受艺术指导，还学习效率指标与观众研究。
在这些不同培训环境中，艺术与意识形态培养日益服从组织绩效逻辑，而经济和管理能力处于这种重组的中心。因此，两个以P开头的词——‘完善’（
）和‘多能性’（
）——成为1980年代文化劳动的标志性用语。它们呼应社会主义‘多技能化’（
）理想，却已转向善于筹措资源与自我管理。

en: Although training initiatives are generally celebrated in the archives (especially for their role in “educating the educators”), some trainees critiqued their centralized design and limited applicability.

Ilarie Curechianu, instructor of artistic brigades in Suceava, noted that irregular scheduling and brief sessions left little room to experiment with new methods. Similarly, Gheorghe Pițu, instructor of artistic ensembles, criticized the absence of practical templates and called for hands-on engagement with repertoires rather than purely theoretical lessons. Such critiques underscore the tension between centralized planning and local realities, but they also point to a methodological insight: media archives, often dismissed as instruments of propaganda, preserve glimpses of site-specific expressions of discontent that are otherwise underregistered in the historical record.
zh: 虽然档案总体上赞扬这些培训举措，尤其肯定其‘教育教育者’的作用，一些学员却批评其集中化设计及有限的适用性。
苏恰瓦艺术宣传队指导员伊拉里耶·库雷基亚努指出，时间安排不规律、课程短促，几乎没有空间试验新方法。艺术团体指导员格奥尔基·皮楚同样批评课程缺乏实用范例，呼吁直接操作演出曲目，而非只讲理论。这些批评凸显中央规划与地方现实之间的张力，也指向一项方法论认识：媒体档案常被视为宣传工具而忽略，却保存了特定地点表达不满的片段；这些声音在其他历史记录中往往很少出现。

en: Other sources echo this broader dissatisfaction and indicate a persistent misalignment between workforce training and the needs of production. One report is particularly scathing: programs, described as “superficial and formalistic,” failed to develop personnel skills and simultaneously reinforced inefficiency and limited adaptability. Training practices reflected a “broader lack of accountability,” being “minor in scope by design, existing only on paper, or limited to brief meetings between a few employees and their section chief at the end of a shift, merely to communicate tasks for the following day.”

The report linked shortcomings in training to persistent quota failures, high defective output, diminished efficiency, and a reduced capacity to adapt to the rapidly changing demands of the national economy.
zh: 其他资料也呼应了这种广泛的不满，并表明劳动者培训与生产需求长期错位。一份报告尤其严厉：被描述为‘肤浅而形式主义’的项目，既未发展人员技能，又强化了低效与适应能力不足。培训实践反映出‘更普遍的问责缺失’：它们‘从设计上就规模微小，只存在于纸面，或仅限于交班时几名员工与科长短暂碰面，只是传达第二天的任务。’
报告将培训缺陷与持续完不成指标、次品率高、效率下降，以及适应国民经济快速变化需求的能力减弱联系起来。

en: To curb these weaknesses and align institutional behavior with economic objectives, “methodological manuals” (

) were introduced. Far from mere bureaucratic formalities, the manuals were designed to familiarize cultural directors with self-financing principles and translate daily operations into the language of economic rationality through step-by-step guidance. An early example of this managerial turn is Iovănescu’s volume

, which framed economic rationality not as an antithesis to creativity but as a necessary condition for it. By extending the language of rationalization across theaters, publishing houses, and museums, the manual embedded self-financing within the cultural field and effectively cast managerial competence as “the rational use of funds” and efficiency as the basis for producing “authentic values.”
zh: 为遏制这些弱点、使机构行为符合经济目标，当局引入了‘方法指导手册’（
）。这些手册远非单纯的官僚形式，设计目的在于使文化主管熟悉自筹经费原则，并通过逐步指导，把日常运作转译成经济理性的语言。这一管理转向的早期例子是约沃内斯库的
，书中并不把经济理性理解为创造力的对立面，而是将其视为创造力的必要条件。手册把合理化语言延伸至剧院、出版社和博物馆，将自筹经费嵌入文化场域，实际上将管理能力表述为‘合理利用资金’，把效率视为生产‘真正价值’的基础。

en: Aimed at instructing institutions in meeting these requirements, another methodological manual defined the late-socialist cultural director as a paradigmatically polyvalent figure: at once scientific manager, public mobilizer, strategic planner, administrator, and pedagogue responsible for ideological alignment, staff coordination, and financial oversight.

Niculescu herself co-authored a practical manual based on directors’ training reports, which codified “scientific management” principles for cultural leadership: from strategic planning and audience research to self-financing optimization and collective organization.

Such manuals illustrate the technocratic reconfiguration of cultural labor under late socialism, where managerial competence became inseparable from, and increasingly defined through, economic performance.
zh: 另一本旨在指导机构满足这些要求的方法手册，将社会主义晚期的文化主管定义为典型的多能人物：他同时是科学管理者、公众动员者、战略规划者、行政人员和教育者，负责保持意识形态一致、协调员工并监督财务。
尼古列斯库本人也参与合著了一本基于主管培训报告的实用手册，把文化领导工作的‘科学管理’原则加以规范化，从战略规划、观众研究，到自筹经费优化与集体组织。
这些手册展现出社会主义晚期文化劳动的技术官僚式重组：管理能力与经济绩效变得不可分割，并日益通过后者来定义。

en: To clarify the relationship of this emerging school of cultural management to market-oriented frameworks, it is useful to distinguish between intent, content, and practice. These reskilling efforts did not explicitly adopt neoliberal corporate models, nor were they designed as such; rather, they emerged within a state-directed and ideologically framed system oriented toward austerity management and administrative efficiency. Yet in practice they cultivated forms of reasoning and conduct that resonate with later managerial and performance-based logics. For instance, while the regime’s emphasis on “perfecting” could be understood in emancipatory terms—as part of the project of forming the “new socialist human” through self-improvement—it also produced a strong emphasis on self-optimization, as well as institutional accountability, that anticipated elements of governance later associated with post-socialist transformations, including individualized responsibility through efficiency-oriented forms of evaluation. This duality resonates with analyses of neoliberal subject formation, in which the individual becomes both manager and managed and internalizes efficiency imperatives as personal obligations.

In this sense, socialist “perfectioning” operated simultaneously as a politically sanctioned moral project and as a mode of self-disciplining that foreshadowed post-socialist forms of entrepreneurial subjectivity.
zh: 为澄清这一新兴文化管理流派与市场取向框架的关系，有必要区分意图、内容和实践。这些技能再塑造努力并未明确采用新自由主义企业模式，也不是按照该模式设计；它们产生于一个国家主导、由意识形态界定的体系内部，目标是紧缩管理和行政效率。但在实践中，它们培养出的推理与行为形式，同后来以管理和绩效为基础的逻辑产生共鸣。例如，体制强调的‘完善’可以从解放角度理解，视为通过自我提升塑造‘社会主义新人’工程的一部分；但它也强烈强调自我优化和机构问责，预示了后来与后社会主义转型联系在一起的某些治理要素，包括通过效率导向的评价将责任个人化。这种两面性与关于新自由主义主体形成的分析相呼应：个人既成为管理者又成为被管理者，并把效率要求内化为个人义务。
从这个意义上说，社会主义的‘完善’同时作为政治认可的道德工程，以及一种自我规训方式而运行，预示了后社会主义时期的企业家式主体性。

en: Finally, this unconventional retraining transformed the role of the socialist cultural director into that of a cultural manager: a figure expected to mobilize scarce resources and reconcile fiscal discipline with ideological expectations. Evidence of this shift lies in the contingent, market-responsive labor regimes of institutions, as well as in the proliferation of managerial training programs and methodological manuals that attuned cadres to administrative efficiency and economic competence. Yet these measures of self-improvement were tightly bound to an expanding apparatus of bureaucratic oversight, which reveals how the self-financing regime depended on, and intensified, practices of (self-)documentation. Institutions were required to act entrepreneurially as well as to continuously record and demonstrate this entrepreneurial conduct before authorities.
zh: 最后，这种不同寻常的再培训把社会主义文化主管转变为文化经理人：他被要求动员稀缺资源，协调财政纪律与意识形态预期。这一转变的证据既体现在机构中具有不确定性、回应市场的劳动制度上，也体现在管理培训项目与方法手册的不断增加上；它们使干部适应行政效率和经济能力的要求。然而，这些自我提升措施与不断扩张的官僚监督装置紧密相连，揭示自筹经费体制如何依赖、并强化了对自身或他者进行记录的实践。机构既被要求像企业家一样行事，也必须持续向当局记录并证明这种行为。

en: As the next section shows, the outcome did not herald a retreat of the state, as decentralization promised on paper, but a fragmented reconfiguration of its presence.
zh: 正如下节所示，结果并未预示纸面上的分权承诺所描绘的国家退却，而是国家存在方式的一种碎片化重组。

en: Decentralization without Autonomy: Tracing the Paper Trail and Keeping Institutions Accountable
zh: 没有自主的分权：追踪文书记录并维持机构问责

en: In early 1988, authorities reporting their visit to the cultural center of Daia Română, a small village in Alba County, found themselves unable to carry out a proper evaluation: “there is no documentation of meeting schedules; there are no minutes of the meetings held, no records of analyses, or of any exchange of views.”

Although two of the center’s nine committee members declared “permanent support” for the cultural agenda, the absence of consistent administrative records undermined these claims, which led inspectors to deem them unsubstantiated. The authorities, in turn, tied these administrative shortcomings to the center’s subpar artistic output and economic performance: they cited “modest achievements” in the

national festival, a series of “formalistic” events, and an unfulfilled self-financing plan. Much to their disappointment, between 1 December 1987 and 17 January 1988, with the exception of weddings (
), no artistic performances had been held.
zh: 1988年初，当局在报告访问阿尔巴县小村达亚罗默讷的文化中心时，发现无法进行适当评估：‘没有会议日程文件；没有已召开会议的纪要，没有分析记录，也没有任何交换意见的记录。’
虽然该中心九名委员会成员中的两位声称对文化议程给予‘永久支持’，缺乏连贯行政记录却削弱了这些说法，检查者因而认为它们没有根据。当局进而把这些行政缺陷同中心不佳的艺术产出和经济绩效联系起来，列举其在
全国艺术节上的‘有限成绩’、一系列‘形式主义’活动，以及未完成的自筹经费计划。令他们大失所望的是，1987年12月1日至1988年1月17日，除婚礼（
）外，这里没有举行任何艺术演出。

en: If, at first glance, Daia Română’s failure appears administrative, presented as a standard case of mismanagement in a peripheral village, it exposes a deeper paradox of late socialism. What was framed as a step toward institutional autonomy soon revealed itself as a deepening of bureaucratic dependence. While decentralization was officially promoted as an empowering mechanism to grant cultural institutions greater freedom for managing resources and responding to local needs, this autonomy was both partial and conditional upon constant proof of compliance. A dense framework of mandatory reporting and periodic state inspections transformed the promise of decentralization into an audit regime. Instead of loosening control, the self-financing regime tightened the state’s grip through paperwork. Every local initiative aimed at meeting the expectations of self-financing had to be recorded and rendered legible to authorities.
zh: 乍看之下，达亚罗默讷的失败似乎只是行政问题，被呈现为边远村庄管理不善的典型案例，实际上它暴露了社会主义晚期更深的悖论。被描述为迈向机构自主的一步，很快显露为官僚依赖的深化。官方将分权宣传为赋权机制，给予文化机构更大自由来管理资源、回应地方需求；然而，这种自主既是局部的，也以不断证明服从为条件。强制报告和定期国家检查构成的密集框架，把分权承诺转化为审计体制。自筹经费体制没有放松控制，而是通过文书工作加强国家掌控。每项旨在满足自筹经费要求的地方举措，都必须被记录下来，使当局能够识读。

en: In its new configuration, decentralization shifted oversight from central authorities to local and regional committees, both enabling and exposing failures, as in the case of Daia Română. Cultural institutions no longer reported directly to the center; their performance was instead assessed locally through a dispersed system of economic and ideological monitoring. Local popular councils were empowered to supervise institutional obligations and became the primary evaluators of reform implementation. In 1988, there were 2,989 such local councils nationally, comprising a total of 62,253 deputy members. Of these, nearly 44 percent were workers, technicians, teachers, doctors, and office employees, while 53 percent were peasants or rural laborers. More than 40 percent of the deputies were women.
zh: 在这一新配置中，分权将监督从中央当局转移到地方和区域委员会，既可能造成失败，也使失败暴露出来，达亚罗默讷即为一例。文化机构不再直接向中央报告，而是由地方通过分散的经济和意识形态监测体系评价绩效。地方人民委员会获权监督机构履行义务，成为改革实施情况的主要评估者。1988年，全国共有2,989个这样的地方委员会，合计62,253名代表。其中近44%是工人、技术员、教师、医生和办公室职员，53%是农民或农村劳动者。女性占代表总数的40%以上。

en: In the same Alba County, for example, a fifty-nine-member cultural committee (comprising cultural activists, workers, and professional and amateur artists) was formed. As Ioan Sicoe, head of the county’s Committee for Culture and Socialist Education, noted, committee members were assigned to specific cultural establishments so that “on-site inspections would be carried out efficiently.”

Methodological consultations were periodically organized, where members presented reports on their involvement in the institutions under their remit. If the stated aim was to “ensure active involvement and for the committee to function as a dynamic, democratic body, responsive to current demands,”

the empowerment of local popular councils produced a twofold effect: it formally expanded participatory decision-making, yet in practice these mechanisms functioned as instruments of oversight, extending central authority through local intermediaries instead of merely redistributing power. Moreover, popular councils were entrusted with overseeing expenditures for socio-cultural activities, which, according to archival reports, accounted for a significant 51 percent of local budgets.

This financial responsibility expanded their role in cultural administration, yet rather than representing an autonomous redistribution of power (and resources), it positioned local councils as key intermediaries through which centrally defined priorities were implemented and monitored.
zh: 例如，在同一个阿尔巴县，成立了一个由文化活动家、工人以及专业和业余艺术家组成的59人文化委员会。县文化与社会主义教育委员会负责人约安·西科埃指出，成员被分配到特定文化机构，以便‘高效开展现场检查’。
委员会定期组织方法咨询会，成员汇报参与其负责机构工作的情况。如果宣示的目标是‘确保积极参与，并使委员会作为一个充满活力、民主、回应当前需求的机构运行’，
那么地方人民委员会获得权力产生了双重效果：形式上扩大参与式决策，实际中这些机制却作为监督工具运行，通过地方中介延伸中央权威，而不只是重新分配权力。此外，人民委员会还受托监督社会文化活动支出；据档案报告，此类支出占地方预算的51%，比重相当可观。
这项财务责任扩大了它们在文化行政中的作用，但与其说代表权力及资源的自主再分配，不如说使地方委员会成为落实并监测中央规定优先事项的关键中介。

en: Decentralization thus shifted risk and responsibility onto local bodies and, in doing so, exposed the limits of local organizational capacity. For instance, at the Tecuci House of Culture, an internal consultation (

) on the role of regional cultural houses was convened but, due to “superficial organization,” was attended by only a single participant—the host institution itself. Representatives from seven other regional institutions failed to appear, some invoking what inspecting authorities wryly noted as “the familiar excuse that the bus did not run that day.”
The meeting ultimately failed to conclude with administrative deliberation but ended with a poetry recital by members of the local Calistrat Hogaș literary circle.
zh: 因此，分权将风险和责任转移给地方机构，也由此暴露地方组织能力的局限。例如，特库奇文化宫召开了一次有关地区文化宫作用的内部协商会（
），但由于‘组织浮浅’，只有一个参与单位出席，即主办机构自身。其他七家地区机构的代表均未到场，一些人使用了检查当局讥讽地称作‘那套熟悉的借口，说当天公共汽车没开’的理由。
会议最终未能以行政审议收尾，而是以当地卡利斯特拉特·霍加什文学社成员的诗歌朗诵结束。

en: Beyond exposing such shortcomings, the retreat from socialism’s hallmark of centralized planning seemed to promise greater creative autonomy. Indeed, some degree of latitude did transpire, as cultural actors found the space to mobilize regional sponsorship networks, while archival traces point to a flourishing of genre experimentation, inter-institutional collaborations, and novel programming strategies across professional music institutions.

This transformation was articulated through what celebrated writer Dumitru Radu Popescu called “demetropolization”—a “new culture” no longer anchored in a single privileged center but produced across a constellation of “local centers,” each capable of generating “culture” independently.

Nevertheless, local autonomy remained carefully delimited by the same central authorities that authorized it. Rather than streamlining the notorious bureaucratic burdens for the managerial class or fostering creative freedom for practitioners, the self-financing regime distended nonessential administrative labor and intensified practices of (self-)monitoring.
zh: 除了暴露这些缺陷，偏离社会主义标志性的中央计划，似乎还承诺给予更大的创作自主。确实出现了一定回旋空间：文化行动者找到动员地区赞助网络的余地，档案痕迹也显示专业音乐机构中的类型实验、跨机构合作和新型节目编排策略蓬勃发展。
著名作家杜米特鲁·拉杜·波佩斯库将这一转变表述为‘去大都会化’：一种‘新文化’不再锚定于唯一享有特权的中心，而是在由多个‘地方中心’构成的星丛中生产，每个中心都能够独立创造‘文化’。
然而，地方自主始终受到批准它的同一中央当局的严格限定。自筹经费体制并未减轻管理阶层臭名昭著的官僚负担，也未促进实践者的创作自由，反而使非必要的行政劳动膨胀，并强化了对自身或他者的监测。

en: Decentralization can thus be seen as a technology of socialist governance. It displaced responsibility downward, and it intensified participatory forms of self-monitoring and individual accountability, in a way that left local institutions with little choice but to document their own performance while remaining bound to central priorities anyway.
